name: Euler CFG++ (alternative, node only)
plain: The second option of the experimental SamplerEulerCFGpp node, with no entry in the sampler list. It feeds a shifted latent into the slope helper, which produces a different formula from the regular CFG++ path. Worth knowing because its last step does not return the guided x0.
math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
d=(x−2D+U)/σ (to_d applied to x−D+U); x'=x+d·(σ'−σ).
Equivalent form with r=σ'/σ: x'=(2D−U)+r(x−2D+U).
Compared with core-euler-cfg-pp in σ-space: x'=D+r(x−U)+(1−2r)(D−U).

props.final_sigma0: No branch. σ'=0 gives x'=2D−U, not D, so the final result has the guidance gap applied twice.
props.flow_const: No branch and no α factors.

providers.author: Extraltodeus
providers.note: distance_wrap(resample=0, cfgpp=True) gives the same Euler step with the x−2x̂+x̂_u slope as core's version=alternative, but registers it in the KSampler list; falls back to plain Euler if the captured negative is all zeros (presets_to_add.py:49).

label: from code
surprise: Final step returns 2D−U rather than D: the guidance gap is added again on the last step.
